what_its_for: Chlorzoxazone is a muscle relaxer used to treat pain and stiffness caused by muscle strains, sprains, and other muscle injuries. It works on your brain and spinal cord to help your muscles relax and reduce discomfort.
how_to_take: Take chlorzoxazone by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 750 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day (every 6 to 8 hours). Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for you. Do not take more than your doctor prescribed. This medicine is usually used for a short time (a few weeks) along with rest and physical therapy.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store chlorzoxazone at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine past its expiration date.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking chlorzoxazone. Alcohol can increase drowsiness and dizziness and raise the risk of serious side effects. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially sleep aids, anxiety medicines, pain relievers, and antihistamines, as they may increase drowsiness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you notice: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark urine, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, unusual tiredness or weakness, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. These could be signs of a serious liver problem. Also call your doctor if your muscle pain does not improve after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Chlorzoxazone usually starts working within 1 hour of taking it. You may feel some relief of muscle pain and stiffness within the first day or two. It works best when used together with rest, physical therapy, and other treatments your doctor recommends.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with extra caution. Older adults are more sensitive to the drowsiness and dizziness this medicine can cause, which raises the risk of falls. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Liver disease: Do NOT use chlorzoxazone if you have liver disease or a history of liver problems. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been well established. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
